brief: A transitional serif for long reading: calm, crisp and bookish, more composed than decorative. Must work in 16-20 px paragraphs and still look good in a large headline.

why.thin: 33 against a stem of 90 gives moderate-to-high contrast with hairlines sturdy enough for text sizes, as the brief requires.
why.stress_deg: -4 is near-vertical, the transitional axis, and calmer than the sans's -10.
why.x_height: 465 of 680 caps is medium-to-large: readable in paragraphs without losing a bookish look.
why.serifs: Bracketed serifs join stems smoothly, which supports continuous reading.
why.terminals: Ball terminals on a, c, f, r and figures are the traditional transitional detail.
why.S: 70 with a floor of 22 keeps serif tips from touching: stems get the floor, and rounds, with no tips, get a little more.
why.proportions: Even widths give the steady rhythm the brief asks for, replacing the wide, display-looking capitals of the first version.
